**Core difference: what history look like after.**

`git merge` — take two branch tips, make new commit with two parents. Nothing rewrite. History show branch existed, when it join.

`git rebase` — replay your commits one by one on top of new base. Each replayed commit is *new commit, new SHA*. Old commits orphaned. History become straight line, looks like you wrote code on top of latest main all along.

```
merge:                      rebase:
A---B---C main              A---B---C main
     \       \                       \
      D---E---M feature               D'--E' feature
```

**Key consequence:** rebase rewrite history. Merge no. That drive most rules.

**Reach for rebase when:**
- Your local feature branch stale, want fresh main under it before finish. `git pull --rebase` daily.
- Cleaning up own messy commits before review. `git rebase -i` — squash "fix typo", "wip", "wip 2" into one real commit.
- Team want linear history, easy `git log`, easy `git bisect`.

**Reach for merge when:**
- Branch already pushed and other people pulled it. Rebase there force them into conflict hell.
- Merging feature into main/shared branch — merge commit record the integration point.
- You want honest record of what happened, including parallel work.
- Conflicts big. Merge = resolve once. Rebase = maybe resolve same conflict at every replayed commit.

**The rule that matter:** never rebase commits that exist on remote shared branch. Push after rebase need `--force-with-lease`, which overwrite other people's basis.

**Practical combo most teams use:**
```
git checkout feature
git rebase main        # tidy, linear, current
git checkout main
git merge --no-ff feature   # explicit merge commit marks feature landing
```
Best of both — clean commits inside feature, visible boundary in main.

**Conflict handling differ:**
- Merge conflict: fix once, `git add`, `git commit`. Done.
- Rebase conflict: fix, `git add`, `git rebase --continue`. Repeat per commit. Escape hatch `git rebase --abort` return to before state.

Turn on `git config --global rerere.enabled true` — git remember conflict resolutions, replay them automatic. Big help during rebase.
